text: In json2html's object branch, line 86 `key = htmlEscape(key)` CLOBBERS the for-in loop variable, and the two subsequent statements then index the original object with the HTML-ESCAPED key: line 92 `isCollapsable(json[key])` and line 97 `json2html(json[key], options)`. For any attacker-supplied JSON object key containing one of & < > ' " (e.g. {"R&D": "secret"}, {"it's": "secret"}, {"a<b": "secret"}), the escaped key ("R&D") no longer names a property of `json`, so `json[key]` evaluates to undefined. `json2html(undefined, options)` then matches NONE of the dispatch branches -- typeof!=='string'/'number'/'boolean', `undefined === null` is false (strict), not `instanceof Array`, and line 80 is `typeof json === 'object'` which is false for undefined -- so it falls through the whole if/else chain and returns the initial `var html = ''` (line 42). Net effect: the viewer silently renders the key followed by ': ' and an EMPTY value, dropping the real value, and also suppresses the collapse toggle (isCollapsable(undefined) is false). Attacker control of a single key name therefore suppresses display of that key's value. Integrity/display-fidelity defect, not code execution -- it matters where this viewer is used to review security-relevant JSON (token scopes, permission objects, audit records), because a field's value can be made invisible to the reviewer. Note it does NOT throw, precisely because line 80 is a `typeof === 'object'` guard rather than a bare `else`. Fix: keep the raw key for indexing and escape only into the display string (e.g. `var keyRepr = htmlEscape(key)` without reassigning `key`).

text: Attacker-controlled JSON string values are rendered as links with `target="_blank"` and NO `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. At line 45 the string is htmlEscaped, then at line 47 `options.withLinks && isUrl(json)` gates line 48: `html += '' + json + ''`. `withLinks` DEFAULTS TO TRUE (line 124 `_tmp_6.withLinks = true`), so this is the out-of-the-box path. When the JSON string is an absolute http(s)/ftp(s) URL accepted by isUrl's regex, the newly opened attacker page receives a live `window.opener` handle to the hosting document and can navigate it (reverse tabnabbing / phishing redirect of the opener). Secondarily, isUrl's regex makes the scheme group OPTIONAL -- `(https?:\/\/|ftps?:\/\/)?` -- so a scheme-less string such as `evil.com` also matches and is emitted as ``, a RELATIVE URL resolved against the hosting page's base, which silently mis-renders the value as a same-origin link. I verified this is NOT an XSS: `"` is escaped to `"` by htmlEscape so the attribute cannot be broken out of (entity decoding happens after attribute tokenization), and the regex cannot match a `javascript:`/`data:` URI because the host-label class `[a-z0-9%-]` excludes `:`, the only other `:` positions are a digits-only port `(:(\d{1,5}))?` and a `/`-prefixed path. Fix: add rel="noopener noreferrer" and require an explicit safe scheme.

text: ReDoS (polynomial/quadratic backtracking) in the `urlRegexp` literal inside `isUrl`, json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.js line 21, applied to attacker-controlled data at line 22. The literal is: /^(https?:\/\/|ftps?:\/\/)?([a-z0-9%-]+\.){1,}([a-z0-9-]+)?(:(\d{1,5}))?(\/([a-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%]+)?)?$/i  -- the sub-pattern `([a-z0-9%-]+\.){1,}` is a nested quantifier (inner `+` under outer `{1,}`, the classic (a+)+ family), and it is immediately followed by `([a-z0-9-]+)?` whose character class OVERLAPS group 1's class (both match [a-z0-9-]), creating cross-group ambiguity. `isUrl` is an :EntryPoint (exposure=reachable, kind=handler) and the regex is tested against its parameter. IMPORTANT SCOPING FOR THE VERIFIER: blowup is NOT exponential, because the mandatory `\.` inside the group is absent from `[a-z0-9%-]`, so every outer iteration must consume exactly one dot and iteration boundaries are deterministic. The residual ambiguity is (number of dots `{1,}` can give back) x (greedy length choices of the trailing `([a-z0-9-]+)?`), i.e. ~O(n^2). Suggested repro: json2html receives a JSON string value of the form ('a.' repeated k) + ('a' repeated m) + one character in NO class (e.g. a space or backslash) to force failure; maximize k*m with k~n/4, m~n/2. At n=50k chars this is ~1e8-1e9 backtracking steps. Impact is a client-side hang/tab freeze (browser plugin), so this is a moderate availability issue, not RCE.

text: Missing URL scheme allowlist before an href sink: isUrl() (json-viewer/jquery.json-viewer.js:20-22) is the ONLY gate deciding whether an untrusted JSON string is interpolated into `<a href="...">` at L48, and its scheme alternation is optional — `/^(https?:\/\/|ftps?:\/\/)?([a-z0-9%-]+\.){1,}([a-z0-9-]+)?(:(\d{1,5}))?(\/([a-z0-9\-._~:/?#[\]@!$&'()*+,;=%]+)?)?$/i` — with the trailing `?` on the scheme group. There is no explicit protocol check (no startsWith('http'), no new URL(...).protocol test, no scheme denylist) anywhere in the scan, so the code relies entirely on an incidental property of the regex's host character class to keep dangerous schemes out of the href. I checked exploitability rather than assuming it: the host component `[a-z0-9%-]` excludes ':' , so a literal `javascript:alert(1)` prefix cannot match the anchored pattern, and although '%' IS in that class (so `javascript%3aalert%281%29.x` does satisfy the regex), browsers do not percent-decode before scheme resolution, making that a harmless relative URL. I therefore report this as a MISSING hardening control with a fragile implicit guard — any future widening of the host class, or removal of the `{1,}` dot requirement, converts it directly into stored DOM XSS at the L48 href. A verifier should re-derive whether any scheme reaches the href on the target browser matrix before treating this as more than hardening.
